what_its_for: Rimantadine is an antiviral medicine used to prevent and treat influenza A (the flu). It works by stopping the flu virus from spreading inside your body. It does NOT work for influenza B or for the common cold.
how_to_take: Take rimantadine by mouth with or without food. If it upsets your stomach, try taking it with food or milk. Take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Do not stop taking it early, even if you start to feel better, unless your doctor tells you to.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 100 mg taken twice a day (once in the morning and once in the evening). For treatment of the flu, it is usually taken for about 7 days. For prevention, your doctor will tell you how long to take it. Children's doses are based on weight and age, so follow your doctor's instructions carefully. If you have kidney or liver problems, or if you are elderly, your doctor may lower your dose to 100 mg once a day.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for the missed one.
storage: Store rimantadine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of any unused or expired medicine safely — ask your pharmacist how.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking rimantadine, as it can increase dizziness and other side effects. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you, since it may cause dizziness or trouble concentrating. Live flu vaccines (like FluMist nasal spray) should NOT be used within 48 hours before or 2 weeks after taking rimantadine, as they may not work properly. Ask your doctor or pharmacist before taking other medicines, including over-the-counter cold or flu remedies.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: seizures or convulsions, severe dizziness or fainting, confusion or unusual behavior changes, hallucinations (seeing or hearing things that are not there), trouble breathing, signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty swallowing. Also call your doctor if your flu symptoms get worse or do not improve after a few days.
when_it_works: If you are taking rimantadine to TREAT the flu, you may start to feel better within 1 to 2 days, but it is important to finish the full course. It works best when started within the first 48 hours (2 days) of flu symptoms. If you are taking it to PREVENT the flu, it helps protect you from getting sick as long as you keep taking it during the time of exposure.
special_populations: Elderly patients (age 65 and older): A lower dose of 100 mg once daily is usually recommended because older adults may be more sensitive to side effects like dizziness and confusion. Kidney or liver problems: Your doctor may lower your dose. Make sure to tell your doctor about any kidney or liver conditions. Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor before taking this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Breastfeeding: This medicine may pass into breast milk. Do not breastfeed while taking rimantadine without talking to your doctor first. Children: Safety and dosing in children under 1 year of age has not been established. Use in children is primarily for prevention of flu; consult your doctor for proper dosing.
